shouldFix.title: frozenReviewFindingExtractor fails open to an empty set for unsupported and mixed positive-count verdict schemas
evidence: The new extractor explicitly says: 'A file that matches neither extracts the empty set.' An unsupported frozen verdict is therefore treated as having no findings rather than making successor authoring refuse.

A concrete unsupported-schema probe with blockers=1, shouldFix=0, advisories=0 and no findings[] or severity arrays takes the empty fallback. An empty register lane then equals the extracted empty set and passes laneCheck despite the frozen verdict declaring one blocker.

The severityArrays branch has the same fail-open edge for mixed schemas. A probe with blockers=[], advisories=[], and shouldFix=2 as an integer count matches the branch, skips the integer by rule, extracts empty, and again lets an empty lane pass despite two declared SHOULD-FIX.
registerCoverageRule.resultIfIncomplete says the successor refuses, but these cases are reported as complete because the extractor silently discards the only evidence that findings exist.

Every actual frozen v8-v16 verdict matches one of the two recognized schemas, all per-lane sets and (lane,id) pairs reproduce exactly, and every FromVN prefix equals the REPAIRED register set. The current data is therefore sound; the defect is the governing fallback, which bounds it to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: A future frozen review schema change, partial writer output, or mixed count/array shape can erase blockers and SHOULD-FIX from the mechanical lineage check without a mismatch. That reopens the exact omission class the new fail-closed coverage rule is meant to prevent.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make an unrecognized verdict schema refuse rather than extract empty. In the severity-array branch, refuse when any skipped integer count is positive unless a recognized combined findings[] array supplies those ids. Permit an empty extraction only for a recognized schema that explicitly proves zero findings, and cross-check any available integer counts against the extracted severity totals.
